label: copy-phase input p early in the recall (recall_idx 1-3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is p, i.e. the model just output p as one of the first few original tokens. 99% of activation mass is on in_tok == p. It never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter step. Magnitude falls off steeply with position: strongest at recall_idx 1, where p was the first original token (53% of mass, ~96% precision, max activations ~4.6). It is weaker at recall_idx 2 (41% of mass), weak and unreliable at recall_idx 3 (6% of mass, ~40% precision), and essentially absent from recall_idx 4 on. A p fed back directly after another p (e.g. p p ...) fires only about half as strongly. It does not fire on p in the original phase or on other tokens. False positives are mostly p inputs at recall_idx 3 (and some at 2) that stay silent.

issues: The basic claims check out: all activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000; nothing on original or delimiter steps), 99.4% of mass is on in_tok == p, and mass by recall_idx is 1: 53%, 2: 41%, 3: 5.7%, 4 and later about 0.

There is a systematic gap the explanation misses: firing depends strongly on how many outputs are still to come (to_go = L-1-recall_idx), not only on recall_idx. Dev precision for p inputs by (recall_idx, L): r=1 is 0.39 at L=3, 0.82 at L=4 and 0.98-1.0 at L>=5. r=2 is 0.00 at L=3, 0.07 at L=4, 0.85 at L=5 and 1.0 at L>=6. r=3 rises steadily with L: 0.00 at L=4, 0.007 at L=5, 0.20 at L=6, 0.55 at L=7, 0.75 at L=8, 0.84 at L=9.

So the false positives are not 'mostly p at recall_idx 3 (and some at 2)' scattered across sequences. They are p inputs in short sequences, where few outputs remain. The claimed '~96% precision at recall_idx 1' holds only for L>=5. A p at recall_idx 2 in an L=3 or L=4 sequence is almost never active.

The test misses on the original predicate confirm this. The false positives (13,700 steps) are dominated by short sequences, e.g. 'p c u z <DEL> *p*' (L=4, recall 1, silent), '1 p 2 <DEL> 1 *p*' (L=3, silent) and 'k m p d <DEL> k m *p*'.
The label overclaims: 'early in the recall (recall_idx 1-3)' leaves out the required condition that at least 2-3 outputs are still to come.
Adding the to_go condition raises test F1 from 0.826 to 0.926, with precision going from 0.723 to 0.913 and mass recall staying at 0.989.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input p within the first ~3 recall steps, but only when at least 2-3 outputs are still to come (silent in short sequences near the end)
